config.title: Counter App

intro.title: Counter App
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Counter App that displays a number and allows users to increment or decrement it with buttons. This project teaches you the fundamental React concept of state management using the useState hook, which lets components remember and update data over time. You'll learn how to create interactive user interfaces by handling click events and updating the component's state, causing the UI to re-render with new values. The main technologies you'll work with include React functional components, JSX for structuring the interface, and event handlers for user interactions. By the end of this lesson, you'll understand how React's state system enables dynamic, responsive applications that update in real-time based on user actions.
intro.usecase: Counter patterns are fundamental building blocks in modern web applications, appearing everywhere from shopping cart quantity selectors and social media like/reaction buttons to inventory management dashboards and form input controls. E-commerce sites use counters for product quantities, social platforms track engagement metrics in real-time, and admin dashboards display live statistics like user counts or sales numbers. As a React developer, you'll implement counter logic in notification badges, pagination controls, timer components, and any interface where users need to increment, decrement, or track numerical values. This pattern teaches essential state management concepts that scale up to complex applications managing multiple dynamic values across components.

objectives: Initialize state variables to manage numeric counter values in React components
Implement event handler functions that modify state based on user interactions
Construct JSX elements that display dynamic state values within component markup
Bind click events to button elements for triggering state updates
Apply the useState hook to create and update reactive data in functional components
Configure increment and decrement operations that manipulate counter state
Render interactive buttons that control the counter's numeric display
Integrate state management with UI elements to create a responsive counter interface

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from 'react' to set up the required dependencies for building a counter app with state management.
steps.hint: Write the import statement at the top of your file. You'll need both React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple items from a module
import { Component, useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: React and useState are imported from the 'react' package, making them available for use in the counter component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package in a single import statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both React and useState from 'react'. You'll need both for creating a functional component with state.

steps.title: Create Counter component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Counter that returns null for now
steps.hint: Define a functional component using either function declaration or arrow function syntax. The component should be named Counter and return null as a placeholder.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create your Counter component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named Counter is created that returns null
successCriteria: Counter component is defined and returns null
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track! Make sure your component is named Counter and returns null for now.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a functional component named Counter that returns null. You can use either function declaration or arrow function syntax.

steps.title: Initialize count state
steps.instruction: Inside your Counter component, create a count state variable initialized to 0 using the useState hook.
steps.hint: Use useState(0) to create a state variable that starts at 0. Destructure it into count and setCount variables.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: creating state for a name
const [name, setName] = useState('John');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have count state initialized to 0 with setter function setCount
successCriteria: useState is called with initial value 0, and the returned array is destructured into count and setCount variables
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start with useState! Make sure you're destructuring into count and setCount variables and initializing with 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: use useState(0) and destructure the returned array into [count, setCount] variables.

steps.title: Define increment handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleIncrement that increases count by 1 using setCount
steps.hint: Define the function inside your component and use setCount(count + 1) to increment the current count value
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleIncrement function is defined that uses setCount to increase count by 1
successCriteria: handleIncrement function is created and uses setCount to increment count
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your handleIncrement function uses setCount to increase the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleIncrement function should use setCount(count + 1) to increment the counter value.

steps.title: Define decrement handler
steps.instruction: Create a handleDecrement function that decreases the count by 1 using setCount.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setCount with count - 1 to decrease the value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleDecrement function is created that decreases the count state by 1.
successCriteria: handleDecrement function is defined and calls setCount to decrease count by 1
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your handleDecrement function calls setCount with count - 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a function named handleDecrement that calls setCount(count - 1) to decrease the counter.

steps.title: Define reset handler
steps.instruction: Create a handleReset function that sets the count back to 0 using setCount.
steps.hint: Use setCount to update the count state to 0. This function will reset the counter to its initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReset function is created that resets the count state to 0
successCriteria: handleReset function is defined and uses setCount to set count to 0
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track! Make sure your handleReset function calls setCount with 0 as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a handleReset function that uses setCount(0) to reset the count state to its initial value.

steps.title: Add JSX container structure
steps.instruction: Return a div container with className 'counter-app' from the Counter component.
steps.hint: Replace the empty div in the return statement with a div that has className='counter-app'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Counter component returns a div with className 'counter-app' as the main container.
successCriteria: The div element has className='counter-app' and serves as the main container for the counter app.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the div has className='counter-app' exactly as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The div needs to have className='counter-app'. Check that you've added the className attribute with the correct value.

steps.title: Display counter value
steps.instruction: Add an h1 element inside the div that displays the current count value.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to display the count state variable inside the h1 element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: displaying a variable in JSX

{score}
steps.expectedOutcome: An h1 element that displays the current count value (0) inside the div.
successCriteria: An h1 element is added inside the div that displays the count state variable using JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using an h1 element and displaying the count variable inside JSX curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: add an h1 element inside the div and use JSX curly braces to display the count state variable.

steps.title: Add increment button with onClick handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text '+' that calls the handleIncrement function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the button element with an onClick prop to wire the event handler.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: a button that calls a function
<button onClick={handleSave}>Save</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button with '+' text that triggers the increment function when clicked
successCriteria: Button element with text '+' and onClick prop calling handleIncrement
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your button has the '+' text and calls handleIncrement on click.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button needs the text '+' and an onClick prop that calls handleIncrement.

steps.title: Add decrement and reset buttons with onClick handlers
steps.instruction: Add two buttons after the increment button: one with text '-' that calls handleDecrement on click, and one with text 'Reset' that calls handleReset on click.
steps.hint: Create two <button> elements with onClick props that call the respective handler functions you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two additional buttons are added: one with '-' text that decreases the counter when clicked, and one with 'Reset' text that resets the counter to 0 when clicked.
successCriteria: Two buttons are added with text '-' and 'Reset' respectively, each with onClick handlers that call handleDecrement and handleReset.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good progress! Make sure both buttons have the correct text ('-' and 'Reset') and that their onClick handlers call the right functions (handleDecrement and handleReset).
steps.feedbackWrong: Not quite right. You need to add two buttons: one with '-' text that calls handleDecrement, and one with 'Reset' text that calls handleReset. Make sure to use the onClick prop.
